A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same online federated continual learning framework and BI-based memory method. All 15 pages of v2 and 19 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments on CIFAR10, CRC-Tissue, KC-Cell and 20NewsGroups, including accuracy and forgetting results in Tables 1–4 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds benchmark results, component ablations, runtime measurements and generated-image examples in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The BI/TTA estimator, class-balanced memory selection, random replay, burn-in, periodic communication and aggregation framework remain. O-FCIL is renamed O-FCL, and Algorithm 1 documents the existing procedure. Testing alternative aggregation strategies does not establish a change to the previously flexible method.

E1.justification: v3 adds CIFAR100, DBPedia and Yahoo Answers while retaining all four original datasets. This substantially expands class coverage in vision and the represented text-classification data; text classification itself was already evaluated in v2.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds distinct FedProx, FedCIL and weighted FedAvg comparisons, including on CIFAR10. It also evaluates FL and generative baselines on retained datasets beyond the original CIFAR10 comparison. ER, CBR and the four alternative uncertainty scores remain.

E3.justification: The main batch size, client count, models and default communication settings remain. New experiments introduce burn-in and communication-frequency sweeps, aggregation alternatives, 8/10/12-augmentation controls, runtime evaluation and subsampling for the added text benchmarks. These expand the evaluation design rather than establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.5 tests burn-in, aggregation, communication frequency and augmentation count. Appendices A.6–A.8 add communication-cost analysis, runtime comparisons and an MFCL generated-image case study addressing failure in the online setting. These analyses were absent from v2.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use three random seeds and retain the same plus/minus reporting in matched benchmark tables. No changed run count, significance test or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported. The added ablation tables provide point estimates without specifying an additional statistical procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive benchmark, baseline, ablation and runtime results. It also revises CRC-Tissue scores: bottom-BI at M=120 changes from A=59.06 and F=23.10 to A=62.33 and F=7.99, without explaining the revision. Matched CIFAR10, KC-Cell and 20NewsGroups table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal online-learning setup, BI estimator and uncertainty/evaluation equations (1–8) remain. No theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is added. The new pseudocode and communication-count calculation document implementation and experimental costs.

C1.justification: The core contributions—online FCL and uncertainty-based replay across modalities—remain. The v3 abstract additionally claims maintained data confidentiality and competitive communication efficiency, extending the stated benefits without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 and the new appendices substantially expand interpretations of augmentation quality, communication tradeoffs and generative-model failure. Section 3.2.2 discusses operation without sharing class information. Medical-domain superiority is narrowed from all cases to most cases; the original TTA cost and estimator-bias limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds execution pseudocode, text-dataset subsampling information and training-time measurements. Architectures, optimizers, hardware and the augmentation list were already documented in v2. Reproducibility remains imperfect: Appendix A.3 reverses the DBPedia and Yahoo Answers sample counts relative to Table 6.

R1.justification: v3 adds Li et al. for FedProx and Zhang et al. for the added text datasets, and explicitly claims the first use of the cited decomposition for FCL memory management. The related-work taxonomy and principal positioning against offline generative approaches remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes, O-FCIL becomes O-FCL, and the conclusion becomes a discussion-and-conclusion section with additional subsections and appendix references. Local wording and explanations are revised, but most introductory, related-work and methodological prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn from four clients to two and receives an expanded caption. The medical tables are merged side by side, the text-results table expands, and v3 adds benchmark and analysis tables, generated-image Figure 5 and an algorithm display. These substantially change the presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 left important component choices and computational practicality largely untested. v3 adds targeted ablations, measured runtimes and broader FL/FCL comparisons, substantially strengthening empirical scrutiny of the same method. Pseudocode also improves transparency. Benefits are tempered by reporting inconsistencies: Appendix A.3 and Table 6 disagree on text-subset sizes, and Figure 3 retains baseline scores unreconciled with Table 5. These limit precision but do not outweigh the stronger empirical foundation.
